newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki seen starting higher post-Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki seen starting higher post-Greenspan.

text.p: Shares were seen opening higher on Wednesday after U.S. markets rallied in response to an air-clearing speech by Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan, brokers said.
"It was a very positive-toned speech," one broker said, predicting a one percent overall gain for the day, while others were more optimistic and forecast a rise of up to two percent.
Nokia rose in New York overnight, but still ended some five markka below its Helsinki close. It was seen playing catch-up and moderating the overall rise at the open, brokers said.
"But the broad market is certainly positive," one said.
It would take a rise of 3.3 percent to put the FOX index back up at its July 17 life-high 1,226.84 points.
Forestries were seen extending their Tuesday gains after the S&P index tracking U.S. paper-makers which rose 2.5 percent overnight.

Bullish debt markets at home and abroad were seen supporting stocks. "Interest rates were headed downwards here yesterday, and U.S. rates fell 12 points," one broker said, referring to the decline in the 30-year Treasury yield.
